paragraphs.context: One summer day in Frog Creek, Pennsylvania, a mysterious tree house appeared in the woods.
paragraphs.mainIdea: The story of the series so far.
paragraphs.simple: Jack and Annie found a magic tree house full of books. If they point to a picture in a book, they can go to that time and place. No time passes at home while they are away.

background.note: Frog Creek is a made-up town. Pennsylvania is a real state in the eastern United States.

paragraphs.context: Jack and Annie eventually found out that the tree house belonged to Morgan le Fay,
paragraphs.simple: The tree house belongs to Morgan le Fay, a magic librarian from Camelot. Jack and Annie have done many missions for Morgan and Merlin. Teddy and Kathleen, two young enchanters, sometimes help them.

background.note: Camelot is King Arthur's castle and kingdom in old British stories.
Merlin is the most famous magician in the King Arthur stories.
Teddy is a young enchanter who works in Morgan's library. Kathleen is a selkie, a magical seal girl from Scottish stories. They first met Jack and Annie in the Merlin Missions books.

paragraphs.context: Now Jack and Annie will use the magic tree house to go on a new kind of mission
paragraphs.simple: This mission will be different from the others. (It is a vacation, not a job.)

paragraphs.context: They were standing on the warm, sunny shore of Frog Creek Lake,
paragraphs.mainIdea: Back from swimming at the lake.
paragraphs.simple: Jack and Annie have been snorkeling in the lake. They are putting away their new swimming things: flippers, masks, snorkels and life vests.

background.note: A snorkel is a short tube. You breathe through it while your face is in the water, so you can look at fish for a long time.
A life vest (life jacket) is filled with light material or air. It keeps you floating if you fall into the water.

paragraphs.context: “It didn’t leak or fog up at all.”
paragraphs.simple: Jack says his new mask was great. No water got in, and the glass did not get cloudy.

paragraphs.context: Jack and Annie stepped into their flip-flops.
paragraphs.simple: They get ready to ride home. Jack says he would love to snorkel around a coral reef one day.

background.note: A coral reef is made by millions of tiny sea animals called corals. Reefs grow in warm, clear, shallow seas and are home to thousands of kinds of fish.

paragraphs.context: Jack strapped the bulky bag to the rack over his back wheel.
paragraphs.simple: Jack ties the big bag to his bike. They put on their helmets and ride away from the lake.

paragraphs.context: “Remember when Randy and Jenny snorkeled around a coral reef last spring?”
paragraphs.simple: Jack remembers that their friends Randy and Jenny saw a coral reef on a trip.

paragraphs.context: they went to a place called Cozumel with their parents,
paragraphs.mainIdea: Annie wants to call their friends.
paragraphs.simple: Annie remembers the place: Cozumel. She wants to phone Randy and Jenny, who should be home by two o'clock.

background.note: Cozumel is an island in the Caribbean Sea, off the east coast of Mexico. It is famous for its coral reefs and is a popular place for snorkeling and diving.

paragraphs.context: Annie reached into her handlebar bag and took out the old cell phone
paragraphs.simple: They stop at the side of the road. Annie takes out their dad's old phone. Randy has sent a text: his family is not coming home until tomorrow.

paragraphs.context: He started up their street, heading for their house.
paragraphs.simple: Jack says it is OK, and they start to ride home.

paragraphs.context: “Jack, stop!” Annie called from behind him.
paragraphs.simple: Annie suddenly calls Jack to stop. She has seen something.

paragraphs.context: Jack stopped his bike and looked back.
paragraphs.simple: Jack stops riding and looks back. Annie is riding fast to catch up with him.

paragraphs.context: She screeched to a halt.
paragraphs.simple: Annie stops her bike very suddenly. She has found a yellow note from Teddy in her bike bag.

paragraphs.context: Teddy must have put it there when we were snorkeling!
paragraphs.mainIdea: How did the note get there?
paragraphs.simple: Annie guesses many times and places when Teddy could have put the note in her bag. She talks fast because she is excited.

paragraphs.context: Please meet me at the tree house as soon as possible.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy asks them to come to the tree house very soon.

paragraphs.context: they turned and rode their bikes between the trees
paragraphs.simple: They ride fast up the street and into the Frog Creek woods. Their bikes bounce over roots and leaves.

paragraphs.context: I hope nothing’s wrong back in Camelot!
paragraphs.simple: Annie is a little worried. Maybe something bad has happened in Camelot.

paragraphs.context: “And Penny!” said Annie.
paragraphs.simple: Jack and Annie name all their friends in Camelot.

background.note: Penny is a little penguin who lives in Camelot. Jack and Annie helped her in an earlier Magic Tree House book.
King Arthur is the king of Camelot in old British stories. In these books, Jack and Annie have helped him before.

paragraphs.context: A freckle-faced teenager with tousled red hair
paragraphs.simple: The magic tree house is back in the oak tree. Teddy, a teenage boy with messy red hair and freckles, leans out of the window.

background.note: Freckles are small light-brown spots on the skin. Many people with red hair have them.

paragraphs.context: Annie and Jack pulled off their helmets
paragraphs.simple: They take off their bike helmets, leave their bikes by the tree and climb up. They give Teddy a hug.

paragraphs.context: “Indeed they do!” said Teddy.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy says yes: Merlin and Morgan have a new mission for them.
paragraphs.tone: Teddy talks in an old-fashioned, polite way. "Indeed" is a word he likes.

paragraphs.context: They want you to have a fantastic time
paragraphs.simple: The mission is to have a great time. This is not like their usual missions.

paragraphs.context: never properly thanked you for all your hard and dangerous work
paragraphs.simple: Merlin and Morgan feel they have not thanked Jack and Annie well enough for all the hard and dangerous things they did.

paragraphs.context: they want to send you on a holiday
paragraphs.simple: Teddy smiles and says they want to thank the children in a special way: by sending them on a holiday.

background.note: In British English, a "holiday" is a trip for fun. Americans call it a "vacation". Teddy comes from Camelot, so he says "holiday". In America, a "holiday" is usually a special day, like Christmas.

paragraphs.context: Then their timing is perfect.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy is happy that the time is just right. He asks where they would most like to go.

paragraphs.context: I do not believe I have heard of that land.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy has never heard of Cozumel. He comes from long ago, so many places are new to him.

paragraphs.context: It’s an island in the Caribbean Sea
paragraphs.simple: Jack explains: Cozumel is an island near the Yucatán Peninsula, and it is part of Mexico.

paragraphs.context: said Teddy, wrinkling his nose
paragraphs.simple: Teddy does not know the word "snorkeling". He moves his nose up because he does not understand.

paragraphs.context: You swim in a lake or ocean and look underwater through a mask.
paragraphs.simple: Jack explains: you swim with a mask on your face and look under the water.

background.note: A snorkel mask covers your eyes and nose. It has a glass window, so you can see clearly under the water.

paragraphs.context: they said the snorkeling was incredible
paragraphs.simple: Their lake is not good for snorkeling, but their friends Randy and Jenny said snorkeling in Cozumel was amazing.

paragraphs.context: He reached into his cloak and pulled out a wand.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy takes out a wand and waves it while he whispers magic words. Slowly, a small book appears on the floor.

background.note: A wand is a thin stick. In stories, magicians and sorcerers hold a wand when they do magic.

paragraphs.context: The cover was a collage of several small paintings and photos.
paragraphs.simple: The cover has many small pictures: a big hotel, a stone pyramid and a person snorkeling.

background.note: A collage is a picture made by putting many small pictures or pieces of paper together.

paragraphs.context: Visit Cozumel and the Yucatán Peninsula!
paragraphs.simple: The back of the book tells visitors what they can do there: stay in a nice hotel, see old Mayan buildings and snorkel in the sea.

paragraphs.context: Annie took their cell phone from her handlebar bag
paragraphs.simple: They hurry down. Annie puts the phone in her pocket, Jack takes the swim bag, and they climb back up.

paragraphs.context: He reached into his cloak and pulled out a green velvet coin purse.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy gives Annie the travel book. Then he gives Jack a small green coin purse.

paragraphs.context: Each of these coins contains a bit of magic.
paragraphs.simple: Teddy explains the three gold coins. If you throw one into the air and make a wish, the wish will come true.

background.note: In many stories, a person makes a wish and magic makes it happen. Often there are three wishes, like the three coins here.

paragraphs.context: The only requirement is that the magic be used to help you have fun.
paragraphs.simple: They may wish for anything, but there is one rule: the magic must help them have fun.

paragraphs.context: They’d never been on a journey without an assignment from Morgan or Merlin.
paragraphs.simple: Jack wonders if there is a real job to do. On every trip before, Morgan or Merlin gave them a task.

background.note: On many earlier trips, magic changed Jack and Annie's clothes so they looked like people of that time and place.

paragraphs.context: Annie pointed at the cover of the travel guide.
paragraphs.simple: Annie points at the picture on the book and wishes to go there. Jack adds the reason: to have a wonderful time.

paragraphs.context: The wind started to blow.
paragraphs.simple: The wind blows and the tree house spins, faster and faster. Then it stops. This is how the tree house travels.

paragraphs.context: Afternoon sunlight flooded into the tree house.
paragraphs.simple: The tree house has landed in a palm tree by a beautiful beach. The sea is bright blue-green, and there is a stone pyramid near the beach, just like the picture on the cover of their travel guide.

background.note: The Maya built stone pyramids with temples on top. There are several small Maya ruins on Cozumel, such as San Gervasio.
A travel guide is a book for tourists. It has maps, photos and information about hotels, restaurants and places to visit.
Coconut palms grow on many tropical beaches. Their seeds, coconuts, can float across the sea to new islands.

paragraphs.simple: Jack is surprised. There are no tourists, no swimmers and no cars at all.

background.note: Experts often say "Maya" for the people and their things (a Maya pyramid) and "Mayan" for their languages. In everyday English, many people say "Mayan" for both.

paragraphs.context: I thought there’d be, you know, luxury spa hotels and fancy restaurants.
paragraphs.simple: Annie expected expensive hotels and restaurants, but she sees none.

background.note: A spa hotel is an expensive hotel where people relax, with things like pools, massages and beauty treatments.

paragraphs.context: Jack looked through their travel guide until he found a photo that seemed to match the deserted shoreline
paragraphs.simple: Jack finds a photo in the guide that looks like this empty beach with the pyramid. He reads the words under the photo.

paragraphs.context: On the southwest Caribbean coast is a nature preserve.
paragraphs.simple: The guide says that on this coast of Cozumel there is a nature preserve: an area where nature is protected.

background.note: The Caribbean Sea is a warm sea between Central America, South America and many islands. Cozumel is on its western side.

paragraphs.context: “Oh, cool! We landed in a nature preserve!”
paragraphs.simple: Annie thinks this explains why the beach looks so wild and natural.

paragraphs.simple: The guide says beautiful coral reefs are close to the beach. New snorkelers can swim there and still see the land.

background.note: The reefs near Cozumel are part of the Mesoamerican Reef, the second-largest coral reef system in the world.

paragraphs.context: “We did come to the perfect place

paragraphs.context: Then maybe check out that pyramid.

paragraphs.simple: A cool wind blows from the sea, and the white sand shines in the sun.

background.note: Fireworks are colored lights that explode in the sky. People in many countries have fireworks displays at big holidays.

paragraphs.simple: At last Jack's excitement is stronger than his fear. The raft rides the waves to the west as if it controls the wind and water. Seagulls fly after it.

paragraphs.simple: The raft goes up and down like a roller coaster. It moves very fast and seems to know where it is going.

background.note: A roller coaster is a fast ride in an amusement park. The writer makes it into a verb: the raft moves up and down like one.

paragraphs.simple: The raft slows down near a far-away beach. The sea is calm and quiet now.

paragraphs.simple: The guide says many tourists go to this coast. There are expensive hotels, good restaurants, Mayan ruins, and hidden holes in the ground full of water.

background.note: The Maya built great cities in southern Mexico and Central America. Many of their old stone buildings, now ruins, are still standing.
In the Yucatán, the ground is soft limestone. Water makes holes in it, and some fill with water. These sinkholes are called cenotes. There are thousands of them.
Guidebooks rate hotels and restaurants with stars. More stars means better and usually more expensive. Five stars is often the top.

paragraphs.simple: Jack thinks the sinkholes sound strange.

paragraphs.simple: The guide says big ships stop along this coast, and ferries carry tourists to Cozumel.

background.note: A cruise ship is a huge ship for vacations. Many cruise ships stop at Cozumel; it is one of the busiest cruise ports in the world.
Today, ferries carry people between Playa del Carmen on the Mexican mainland and Cozumel. The trip takes less than an hour.

paragraphs.context: “We can take a ferry back to Cozumel.

paragraphs.simple: Annie thinks the boats have stopped for the night. The sun is going down behind the cliff.

paragraphs.simple: A photo shows Mayan dancers. Jack thinks the park is about how Mayans lived long ago.

background.note: Maya kings and nobles wore tall headdresses decorated with bright feathers, especially the long green tail feathers of the quetzal bird.

paragraphs.simple: The guide says the park has big music-and-dance shows about Mayan history. A path goes from the park to the hotels.

background.note: Some real parks on this coast, such as Xcaret, have large evening shows about Mayan and Mexican history and culture.
